statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-40355: in MIT krb5 1.18 and later, an application that calls gss_accept_sec_context() on a system with a NegoEx mechanism registered in /etc/gss/mech can be made to dereference a null pointer in parse_nego_message() by an unauthenticated remote attacker, terminating the process. MIT fixed it in krb5 1.22.3 (https://mailman.mit.edu/pipermail/kerberos-announce/2026q4/000212.html) with https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/2e75f0d9362fb979f5fc92829431a590a130929f, backported to the 1.22 branch as https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/acea6182e46fff3d1d64a3172cdff307b07ca441, which is in the krb5-1.22.3-final tag and not in krb5-1.22.2-final. Alpine lists it under 1.22.3-r0 in the 3.23-stable main/krb5 APKBUILD secfixes. This owner's builds for Alpine 3.23 are 1.22.1-r0, whose libkrb5 reports krb5-1.22.1-final and which is affected, and 1.22.3-r0, whose libkrb5 reports krb5-1.22.3-final and which is fixed, on both x86_64 and aarch64.

CVE-2026-40355: in MIT krb5 1.18 and later, an application that calls gss_accept_sec_context() on a system with a NegoEx mechanism registered in /etc/gss/mech can be made to dereference a null pointer in parse_nego_message() by an unauthenticated remote attacker, terminating the process. Debian fixed it for trixie in krb5 1.21.3-5+deb13u1 (DSA-6293-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-40355), which applies the upstream fix https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/2e75f0d9362fb979f5fc92829431a590a130929f. All three builds of this owner currently published for Debian 13, on amd64 and arm64, are built from that Debian source, and the changelog shipped in each libgssapi-krb5-2 package records the fix. The range ends at the lowest of them.
